doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1937 Paris saxophone session with Hawkins, Combelle and Ekyan
summary: Carter fondly remembers Alix Combelle and Andre Ekyan, who recorded with him and Coleman Hawkins.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I would be remiss if I didn’t bring up the historic recording session of April 1937 in Paris with the four saxophones, the first time you worked with just a saxophone group like that. Your friend, Coleman Hawkins, was the other American on the tape. Well, actually, there were two. There was Tommy Benford [phonetic] on drums.
And then you were paired with the two French saxophonists, Alix Combelle and . . . who was the other one? André Ekyan.

Thank you. Oh, my memory failed me at the moment, too, and I was very fond of both of these guys. In addition to being fine saxophonists, fine musicians, they were fine fellows, as they would say over there. But they were lovely guys, and we spent a lot of time together. We developed a very lovely friendship with Alix Combelle and André Ekyan.
